rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~92% for 25bp / ~9% for 50bp, pause priced out (CME FedWatch via Reuters, Nov 11); ECB Dec ~89% (Nov 4); BoJ Dec ~80%; BoC Dec ~34%; BoE 4.00%, RBA 4.85%
rows.read: Markets now treat a December Federal Reserve hike as close to certain, and a second hike early next year as more likely than not. Fed officials keep leaning that way, which widens the gap between US rates and most others. Japan and the euro area are expected to hike in December too, but that is already priced.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Australia new home loans −15.5% q/q in Q3 (fcst ~−8%), investor loans −32%; UK Q3 GDP Thu 1:00 AM CT, fcst +0.7% q/q; euro-area Q3 GDP 2nd estimate Fri 4:00 AM CT
rows.read: Australian home lending slumped in the third quarter, a sign high rates there are biting hard. The US economy still looks firmer than Australia's, Canada's or New Zealand's, a split that favours the dollar. UK growth figures on Thursday are the next big read.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US Oct CPI +0.4% m/m (fcst +0.3%), core +0.3% (fcst +0.2%); US PPI Fri 7:30 AM CT fcst +0.4% m/m, core +0.3%; Japan PPI Wed 5:50 PM CT fcst 6.5% y/y
rows.read: US inflation is running at roughly twice the Fed's goal, and no new figures landed overnight to change that. That keeps the Fed hiking, which supports the dollar and weighs on gold. US producer prices on Friday are the next check.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: USD/JPY ~158.72, USD/CHF ~0.8258, AUD/USD ~0.6870 in Asia; Brent ~$92.5 on Hormuz attacks
rows.read: Asian markets stayed calm overnight, so there was little demand for safe havens. The franc and the yen stayed weak against the dollar as a result. Tanker attacks in the Gulf are the main thing that could change the mood quickly.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$92.54 (+1.15% vs Tue settle $91.49), WTI ~$86.68; Brent $116.72 at the Oct 30 close; API crude stocks +9.0M bbl
rows.read: Oil bounced off its lowest level in two months as attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz continued. Prices are still far below October's peak, which eases the energy bill for Japan and the euro area. Firmer oil gives the Canadian dollar a little support.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Nov 3: hedge funds for USD, JPY, AUD, GBP; against NZD, CAD, EUR; 4-week change NZD −22K, EUR −34K contracts; next report Friday
rows.read: Hedge funds lean toward the dollar and the yen and against the kiwi, the Canadian dollar and the euro, with big recent additions to bets against the kiwi and the euro. The dollar's rise this week has gone with those bets, so there is no sign of a squeeze. The next weekly report is due Friday.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: US 10-year auction Nov 10: $42B at 5.020%, bid-to-cover 2.46 (6-auction avg 2.60), indirects 61.2%; 10-year ~4.98% at Tuesday's close; $25B 30-year auction Thu
rows.read: Weak demand at two US government bond sales this week pushed long-term US borrowing costs up, which supports the dollar for now. The worry is that buyers want more pay to hold US debt. A 30-year bond sale on Thursday is the next check.
